answer: Spectral neighborhood fingerprinting. Each agent's peer set is hashed into a coarse cipher sketch of neighbor-neighbor links, weighted by interaction timber (link age and traffic). New agents join only if their sketch's spectral gap matches the local cluster's, recomputed each epoch. A sybil farm's fabricated links produce anomalous spectra, so each identity requires sustaining real bidirectional traffic across ~8 distinct neighbors for 4 epochs before admission—roughly 30+ hours of genuine coordination per identity, a fable of cheapness.
